Definition: from a derivative of G5531 and G3781; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person:--debtor.
BiblicalUsage: A debtor is one who owes, and Jesus tells of two debtors, one owing five hundred pence and one fifty, and both are forgiven. The unjust steward calls in his master's debtors one by one and cuts what they owe. The word appears in the Greek text with a spelling that differs by a single letter from the dictionaries' form.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus chose debtors for His picture of forgiveness because every one of us owes more than we can pay.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
